note: Shows one progression worked several ways: heard as arpeggios with only the roots played, the shapes, strummed in time over a band, then improvised over with each chord's 3rd lit. Same four chords, four different tools and tasks.

exercise.title: I-V-vi-IV in G, four ways
exercise.focus: G-D-Em-C · roots by ear · shapes · strumming at 80 · 3rds over each chord
exercise.why: Working one progression from several sides makes it something you hear and own, not just four shapes in a row.

sections.text: I-V-vi-IV is under more pop songs than any other four chords, so it repays knowing from every side.
Press Play and listen to one pass of the arpeggios. Then play only each chord's root on the low strings, one note per bar: G, D, E, C. Done when you change on the bar line without looking.
Play the four open shapes in order, four slow strums each.
Strum down, down-up, up-down-up over the drums and bass at 80, one bar per chord. Done at four clean passes in a row.
Improvise in G major near the open chords, and land on each chord's 3rd as it arrives: {{b}} over G, {{f-sharp}} over D, {{g}} over Em, {{e}} over C.
